page.overview:
Who is Pagoda-Bearing Heavenly King Li Jing?

Three days after his son Nezha was born, he proved himself to be a menace by overturning the Dragon King's palace and trying to kill a dragon to use its tendons as a belt. He attempted to kill Nezha, who instead killed himself in rage to return his bones to his father and his skin to his mother.

After dying, Nezha was resurrected by the Tathagata Buddha and eventually began wanting vengeance against his father. King Li Jing pled for mercy from the Buddha, who gifted him a size-changing treasure pagoda filled with openwork carvings and śarīras. Since the pagoda represented the Buddha, Nezhas want for revenge was pacified at the sight of it.
